newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Transport ministers to tackle air traffic issues.
newsitem.headline: Transport ministers to tackle air traffic issues.

text.p: EU transport ministers will tackle the complicated world of European air traffic management and safety on Saturday, the second day of their two-day informal meeting.
The Dutch presidency's press briefing note lists five draft proposals, from three different institutions, providing the basis for discussions.

The proposals include the European Commission's air traffic management White Paper COM(96)57, its proposal for a directive including a mandate for Community membership of Eurocontrol and its proposal for a Council decision including a mandate for the Commission to negotiate the creation of a European Aviation Safety Authority.

The two others are a proposal from the European Civil Aviation Conference (ECAC) on institutional strategy for air traffic management in Europe, including a beefed up Eurocontrol, and a proposal from the permanent commission of Eurocontrol itself, to revise the convention which establishes its legal framework of operation.
The Dutch distil the issues into three, namely:
-- the institutional strategy for European air traffic management;
-- the Community's role in a restructured Eurocontrol and
-- institutional aspects linking aviation safety and traffic management.

On the second point, the Dutch presidency wants ministers to discuss what benefits would accrue from Community membership of Eurocontrol, how membership might affect existing members' voting rights and the efficiency of decision-making.
The presidency also raises the possibility of setting up a high-level working group to discuss the many inter-related aspects of the issue.
